# MiniMax All In One

## Overview

Use this skill as one consolidated routing layer for the public MiniMax skill set. It combines the compact capabilities from 17 MiniMax skills into a single entrypoint so ChatGPT can decide which MiniMax-style workflow to apply without switching between separate skill folders.

This consolidated skill is designed as a practical meta-skill. It does not claim to be a byte-for-byte mirror of every upstream nested file. It contains the compact skill instructions generated from the public MiniMax skill catalog plus upstream links in the bundled references.

## Operating Rule

First classify the user's request into one or more capability domains, then follow the relevant workflow below. For cross-domain tasks, compose the workflows in a sensible sequence and state the execution order before producing the final result.

Default sequence for multi-domain builds:

1. Requirements and architecture.
2. UX and frontend or mobile implementation.
3. Backend and data integration.
4. Documents, slides, spreadsheets, or media assets.
5. Validation, testing, accessibility, release checklist, and handoff.

## Domain Workflows

### Web Frontend

Use the frontend workflow for React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, premium UI, landing pages, dashboards, animated interfaces, persuasive copy, p5.js, Three.js, canvas visuals, and MiniMax-generated media asset planning. Prioritize polished layout, responsive behavior, clear component structure, accessibility, and implementation-ready code.

When the user asks for frontend work, produce the smallest complete artifact that solves the request. For UI design, describe information architecture, component hierarchy, styling system, motion behavior, and implementation steps.

### Full Stack and Backend

Use the fullstack workflow for REST APIs, authentication, authorization, database schema, server-side architecture, real-time features, integrations, environment variables, deployment readiness, and production hardening. Start with requirements, then define architecture, endpoints, data models, error handling, auth flows, and validation strategy.

For full-stack requests, connect backend decisions to frontend integration points. Include API contracts and failure states when relevant.

### Mobile Development

Use Android, iOS, Flutter, or React Native routing based on the platform the user requests. If the user does not specify a platform, choose the framework that best matches the deployment target and explain the choice briefly.

For Android, emphasize Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Material Design 3, Gradle, permissions, accessibility, performance, and adaptive layouts.

For iOS, emphasize SwiftUI, UIKit, SnapKit where relevant, safe areas, touch targets, navigation, Dynamic Type, Dark Mode, Apple HIG, and accessibility.

For Flutter, emphasize widgets, state management with Riverpod or Bloc, GoRouter navigation, testing, localization, and performance.

For React Native or Expo, emphasize components, navigation, styling, forms, networking, state management, native capabilities, SDK upgrades, CI/CD, and performance.

### Shader and Generative Visuals

Use shader routing for GLSL, ShaderToy-style effects, ray marching, signed distance functions, procedural patterns, lighting, particles, volumetrics, post-processing, water, terrain, fractals, and simulation effects. Prefer clear shader structure: uniforms, coordinate normalization, signed distance fields or noise primitives, lighting model, animation time, and post-processing.

When producing shader code, include explanation of the math only where it helps implementation.

### Documents and Office Files

Use the document workflows when the user asks for PDFs, PowerPoint, Excel, spreadsheets, or DOCX documents.

For PDF requests, classify the task as create, fill, reformat, merge, inspect, or export. Preserve print-readiness, typography, page hierarchy, and form-field intent.

For PPTX requests, classify the task as create, edit, read, or extract. Use a deck structure with cover, agenda or TOC where appropriate, content slides, section dividers, summary, and speaker-oriented flow.

For XLSX or CSV requests, classify as create, read, analyze, edit, validate, formula work, or financial formatting. Preserve formulas, formatting, validation rules, and workbook structure when editing existing files.

For DOCX requests, classify as create, fill, edit, format, validate, or template application. Preserve document structure, headings, numbering, tables, and professional formatting.

### Vision Analysis

Use vision routing for image description, OCR, UI mockup review, chart extraction, object detection, layout analysis, and screenshot interpretation. Separate observed facts from inference. For charts or tables, state uncertainty and avoid inventing values that are not visible.

### Media, Music, Stickers, and Multimodal Content

Use multimodal routing for MiniMax-style text-to-speech, voice cloning planning, voice design, music generation, image generation planning, video generation planning, start-end frame planning, subject reference, scene planning, media conversion, concat, trim, and FFmpeg-oriented workflows.

For music generation, clarify the mode implicitly: basic song generation, instrumental, cover, lyric refinement, prompt refinement, structure planning, playlist generation, or buddy singing. Produce lyrics, style prompt, structure, and iteration notes when useful.

For GIF sticker generation, plan four animated stickers from the source subject. Include style direction, caption set, animation action, and prompt-ready descriptions.

## Composition Rules

When a request spans multiple domains, do not answer as separate unrelated sections. Build a single coherent delivery plan. Example: for a SaaS app with landing page, backend, dashboard, spreadsheet export, and pitch deck, route through fullstack-dev, frontend-dev, minimax-xlsx, and pptx-generator in that order.

When the user asks for implementation, provide concrete code, schema, commands, or file structure instead of generic advice.

When the user asks for a plan, produce a structured roadmap with milestones, dependencies, risks, and acceptance criteria.

When the user asks for design or creative output, include prompts, visual direction, asset specs, and review criteria.

When the user asks for document or file generation and a tool is available in the environment, use the relevant artifact tooling rather than only describing the file.

## Quality Gate

Before finalizing, check these points:

- The selected domain matches the user request.
- Cross-domain dependencies are ordered correctly.
- Outputs are implementation-ready or directly usable.
- Accessibility, validation, testing, and edge cases are included when relevant.
- For generated media or design prompts, the intended style, subject, format, and constraints are explicit.
- For documents and office files, the final structure is professional and consistent.
